rawFindings.title: Strict global-return programs are treated as non-strict
rawFindings.explanation: The new Program context validity check only looks at the global scope's `isStrict` flag. When `ecmaFeatures.globalReturn` is enabled, ESLint creates an implicit function scope for the program body, so a top-level `"use strict"` directive makes `scope.childScopes[0].isStrict` true while `context.getScope().isStrict` for Program remains false. As a result, `no-invalid-this` no longer reports invalid top-level `this` in strict CommonJS/global-return code.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the globalReturn implicit-scope check, e.g. compute `scope` and set `valid` false when `context.ecmaFeatures.globalReturn && scope.childScopes[0].isStrict`.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: With rule `no-invalid-this` enabled and parser options `{ ecmaFeatures: { globalReturn: true } }`, input `"use strict"; console.log(this);` produces no lint error, but `this` is invalid in that strict implicit function scope.
